script.title: Understanding Motion: Distance, Speed, and Acceleration
script.subtitle: Master the physics of movement from rest to constant acceleration.

steps.body: Identify if an object's position changes relative to a fixed reference point.
Use formulas like v = s/t for speed and a = (v-u)/t for acceleration.
Convert numerical data into Distance-Time or Velocity-Time graphs to see patterns.

script.example: A car starts from rest (u=0) and reaches 20 m/s in 5s. Find acceleration. a = (v-u)/t = (20-0)/5 = 4 m/s².
script.ctaBody: Solve the NCERT back exercises to lock in these formulas.
script.videoPrompt: A 3D car racing along a straight track with glowing vectors showing velocity and acceleration.

topics.heading: Describing Motion: Distance and Displacement
topics.explain: Distance is the total path covered, while displacement is the shortest straight line between start and end. Think of distance as the winding road you drive and displacement as a bird's flight path.
bullets: Distance is a scalar quantity (magnitude only).
Displacement is a vector quantity (magnitude + direction).
Displacement can be zero if you return to the starting point.
topics.example: A runner goes 4m North then 3m East. Distance = 7m; Displacement = 5m (using Pythagoras).
topics.visual: A dotted winding line (distance) vs a solid straight arrow (displacement) on a grid.

topics.heading: Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion
topics.explain: Uniform motion occurs when an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time. Non-uniform motion is like a car in city traffic, speeding up and slowing down randomly.
bullets: Uniform motion produces a straight line on a Distance-Time graph.
Non-uniform motion produces a curved line on a Distance-Time graph.
topics.example: A cyclist covering 5m every second is uniform; covering 2m, then 5m, then 1m is non-uniform.
topics.visual: Two clocks: one with a steady ticking hand and one with a jumping hand.

topics.heading: Speed and Velocity
topics.explain: Speed is how fast you move, but velocity is speed with a specific direction. It is like saying '50 km/h' (speed) versus '50 km/h towards North' (velocity).
bullets: Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time.
Velocity changes if either speed or direction changes.
topics.example: A car travels 100km in 2h. Average speed = 100/2 = 50 km/h.
topics.visual: A speedometer needle moving alongside a compass needle.

topics.heading: Acceleration
topics.explain: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. It is like a runner's burst of speed at the start of a race to gain momentum.
bullets: Positive acceleration means speeding up; negative (retardation) means slowing down.
topics.example: Velocity increases from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4s. a = (30-10)/4 = 5 m/s².
topics.visual: A 3D ball rolling down a slope, with a growing arrow representing acceleration.

topics.heading: Equations of Motion
topics.explain: These three mathematical formulas describe the relationship between distance, time, velocity, and acceleration for uniform acceleration.
topics.visual: Three glowing mathematical equations floating in a dark space.

script.misconception: Students often think distance and displacement are the same. Correction: Displacement is only the straight-line gap; it can be zero even if distance is huge.
script.examTip: Always write the SI units (m, s, m/s, m/s²) in your final answer to avoid losing half a mark.
